title: Smart Working: Work Flexibility Without Constraints
eligible_reason: Randomized field experiment (smart working one day a week) in a large Italian company: every treated worker starts at the same calendar date. In data_long_282.csv and data_252_long_leaves.csv, post = 0 only in Month0 and post = 1 in Month1-Month9 for both arms (treated 180/165 workers, controls 102/87), so there is a single adoption cohort. The survey DiD (AA_did.csv) is a two-wave pre/post comparison. The two-cohort rule fails for every specification; not a near-miss.
design_notes: Worker-month panels for objective outcomes (productivity, leave days; 10 months, Month0 = pre) and two survey waves (baseline and endline) for self-reported and supervisor-reported outcomes. Table 4 col 3: lm(Days or scale(productivity) ~ Treatment*post + factor(Cod_num_worker) + factor(time)); col 4: Treatment*factor(time) event-time path around the common start. Table 5-6: lm(scale(y) ~ Treatment*post + factor(Cod_num_worker), weights = Weights) on two waves, plus cross-sectional post-period regressions of y on Treatment with and without demographic controls. Tables 7-9 and Appendix D-G: triple interactions with Female, Team_1_0, km, children, other_treated (subgroup-by-treatment). Figures 2 and 5 (Stata): reg y treatment##i.month.
estimators_reported: TWFE 2x2 DiD with common start (worker and month FE)
